sentences: I see 4 and 3, swap them. Then 4 and 2, swap. Then 4 and 1, swap. Each step moves the big number right.
Starting at index zero, compare each pair. Since 4 is bigger every time, it swaps rightward, pushing smaller numbers leftward one by one.
The if checks if left is bigger than right. 4 is bigger than everything, so it keeps swapping until the array looks sorted like 1, 2, 3, 4.
Loop runs j equals zero, one, two. That covers all adjacent pairs. After checking every pair once, the whole array should be in order.
First compare a[0] and a[1]: 4 and 3, swap to 3, 4. Next compare 4 and 2, swap. Next compare 4 and 1, swap. Now it reads 3, 2, 1, 4? Wait, no, I think it becomes 1, 2, 3, 4.
